quest.title: The Other Side of Isle and Sea
quest.description: You discover a strange mural in the Golden Apple Archipelago...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6, Mora x30000

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? Look, there's some sort of... drawing on this stone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like a ship with lots of people on it... meeting a disaster at sea...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't read this very well... Either way, let's make of note of this mural first, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, over here! There's a mural here too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's this... looks like five... pillars? Or are those five cups of water? Paimon wonders which it is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, let's record it down anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Over here! There's a mural here as well!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like a broken ship... and one group of people saving another...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's not totally sure what it means, but let's record this mural down first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like we've found another mural.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This one seems to show a mountain... with a special symbol on it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's not totally sure what it means, but let's record this mural down first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? Look, there's some sort of... drawing on this stone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks like it shows people getting ready to board a ship.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't know what all this means, but let's record this mural down first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon never thought that there'd be a place like this here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? There's a journal here, too... Let's see what it says.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It says that there will be a gap in the fog around the northern island at noon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well then, why don't we do as the journal says and visit that northern island at noon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe we'll find something new...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This mark... looks like the same spot that was on the journal we found.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe that journal and the mural were left by the same group of people!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, we can't make complete sense out of the story these murals depict just by looking at them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe there might be similar murals on the surrounding islands nearby...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's look around and see what we can find!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, it feels as though these murals are hiding some other message. If only we could get someone to help us decipher it...

choices.text: Perhaps we should put up a commission at the Adventurers' Guild.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! If we do that, and the murals turn out to be clues to some treasure, aren't we just giving it up for free?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That won't do! Let's look for... oh, let's go look for a researcher and get them to help us out!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Paimon's heard people say that you can normally find researchers in the library, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go back there and try our luck, shall we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who knows, we might just find the researcher we need there!

choices.text: Let's rope a researcher into this business, shall we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, that would be best. But where would we find one...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we've recorded all these murals down. If we connect them, we should be able to put the pieces together.

talks.objective: Return to Mondstadt and look for a researcher

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: Hello, friend. Is there anything I can do for you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you a researcher?

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: Haha, I suppose I count. Strictly speaking, I am a "wandering scholar," but I suppose that is merely a subset of "researcher."

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: Well, then. Have you encountered a problem that you need a "researcher" to help solve?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, here's what happened...

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: Islands out at sea... and murals that you found there. How fascinating.

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: So you're looking for a researcher who can help you decipher those murals, I gather?

choices.text: Are you willing to help us out?

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: Of course, I have never rejected an opportunity to study the unknown.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: Now then, let us not delay. Could I have a look at those murals?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Here are the ones we recorded down.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: Oh, not bad, not bad at all. My apologies, please give me a moment to think...

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: Hahaha. From the look of things, you must be highly-experienced adventurers.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: However, I would say that these stories of the unknown are the greatest possible remuneration for me. You need not pay me anything else.

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: Hmm. The contents depicted by these murals are not difficult to decipher in and of themselves. I cannot quite put them all in order yet, but I think there should be no problem if we just tried to understand them one by one.

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: First, we have this mural, which depicts a group of people who were shipwrecked.

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: After they were shipwrecked, they must have drifted to the island where you encountered the murals.

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: They then stayed on that island.

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: As for this mural, it shows five objects with five different markings within them.

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: Just like five cups filled with water, with each one containing a different amount of it.

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: This sort of artwork usually hints at a change in the state of something.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: However, I cannot guess at what this "something" is exactly.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: Still, if this is an island in the middle of the ocean, then this "something" could always be "seawater."

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: Next, let's look at this mural.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: After yet another shipwreck, this island welcomed some new "guests."

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: This should be the first batch of people attempting to rescue the second. Also, if you'll have a look at the wreckage depicted here...

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: The first mural only hints at their situation, but this mural goes into quite a lot of detail as to the wrecked ship.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: Perhaps this particular shipwreck meant something unusual to the people who wound up on this island.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: Then we come to this mural.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: Here, I'm sure you can observe that this mountain has been specially marked out.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: I suspect that this place must have been important to these people.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: Finally, we come to this one. Clearly, they found some way to leave this island and thus departed.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: The story the murals tell should be as such.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: It was nothing. In fact, I have always been quite interested in this sort of research.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: Thank you for bringing me this story and these murals. I never thought that I would encounter such things in Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: Perhaps I should take some time out to walk around outside...

choices.text: Why did they have to use murals, though?

response.speaker: Sayid
response.text: Sometimes, images are more intuitive than language when it comes to recording and transmitting information.
